title: About
text:
This project combines historical and real-time financial data with AI to produce automated research reports for US growth stock investors. By feeding macroeconomic indicators, equity market data, and commodity prices into an AI model, each report identifies historical patterns, draws parallels to current conditions, and highlights risks and opportunities for growth-oriented portfolios.
All charts and visualizations in the reports are created by the author — the AI generates only the written analysis.

title: Market Research
text:
The Euphoria Illusion: Navigating Record Equities and Geopolitical Shocks in Mid-2026
Over the past three months, global markets have displayed a striking resemblance to the late-stage expansion phases of 1999 and 2021, characterized by soaring equity indices, extreme commodity volatility, and resilient but rising yields. The MSCI World Index surged to 4807.46 by the end of July 2026, driven by relentless AI capital expenditure, while Brent crude spiked to $96.13 amid escalating US-Iran military strikes. Gold has established a staggering new paradigm above $4,000, hitting $4080.40 in July, reflecting deep-seated geopolitical hedging rather than pure monetary debasement. Meanwhile, global yields have normalized but remain elevated, with the US 10-year yield settling at 4.56% in July, echoing the late-1990s environment where strong nominal growth and geopolitical risk premiums coexisted with euphoric equity valuations.
The domestic equity market is currently pricing in a technological utopia. The S&P 500 closed at 7449.98 and the Nasdaq 100 reached 28388.32 at the end of July 2026. This euphoria is best quantified by the S&P 500 trailing P/E ratio, which stands at 28.49 in July 2026. This valuation metric is flashing the same late-1999 and early-2000 dot-com bubble signals, where multiples detached from traditional gravity and were fueled by a paradigm-shifting technology. Just as the internet rewired expectations then, generative AI is currently justifying premium multiples for tech giants and semiconductor ecosystems, creating a melt-up dynamic that strongly mirrors the 2021 liquidity-fueled peak.



Performance of Major US Stock Indices


Beneath this equity euphoria lies a complex macroeconomic landscape. GDP growth held at a respectable 2.1% in the first quarter of 2026, while the unemployment rate remained steady at 4.2% as of June 2026. However, inflation remains stubbornly sticky, with the CPI YoY hovering at 3.9% in June 2026. This environment forces the Federal Reserve to maintain a cautious stance, with the target rate sitting at 3.75% since December 2025. Consequently, the current 2Y/10Y yield spread of +0.37% (4.19% vs 4.56%) in July 2026 resembles the curve dynamics of early 1995 or late 1999, where the market normalized after an inversion and began pricing in sustained nominal growth and inflation persistence rather than an imminent recession. Credit markets are echoing this complacency; the BofA High Yield Option-Adjusted Spread is remarkably tight at 2.77% in July 2026, and the VIX sits at a subdued 17.5, indicating that investors are entirely dismissive of downside tail risks.
The geopolitical reality, however, threatens to shatter this soft-landing narrative. The ongoing US-Iran conflict, marked by 13 consecutive nights of strikes, has fundamentally altered the energy complex, pushing Brent crude to $96.13 in July 2026. This dynamic heavily mirrors the 1973 and 1979 oil shocks, where Middle Eastern hostilities caused energy prices to spike violently. For growth investors, the relevance of the 1970s energy crisis is a stark warning: sustained high oil prices act as a regressive tax on the consumer and reignite headline inflation, which historically forces central banks to crush long-duration growth assets to preserve currency stability. Gold’s flight to $4080.40 in July 2026 underscores the institutional awareness of this geopolitical fragility.



Brent Oil Prices


Despite these macro headwinds, the sheer earnings power of the AI infrastructure buildout is keeping the broader market afloat, driving global indices to record highs. The market is currently bifurcating between speculative, unprofitable growth and companies with tangible, cash-flow-generating technological moats. As we navigate this unique intersection of dot-com-style valuations and 1970s-style energy shocks, we must carefully weigh the asymmetric risks and opportunities.



MSCI World Equity Index


Risks * Geopolitical Energy Shock & Inflation Resurgence: The ongoing US-Iran conflict has pushed Brent crude to $96.13 as of July 2026. If this escalates into a prolonged supply shock rather than a temporary disruption, headline inflation—which already stubbornly sat at 3.9% in June 2026—could rapidly re-accelerate, forcing the Federal Reserve to abandon its easing cycle and severely compressing the multiples of long-duration growth stocks. * Valuation Extremes and Market Complacency: The S&P 500 trailing P/E ratio of 28.49 in July 2026 approaches the absolute peaks of the 1999 dot-com bubble. Combined with a subdued VIX at 17.5 and remarkably tight high-yield credit spreads at 2.77%, the market is pricing in a perfect soft landing and uninterrupted AI earnings growth, leaving zero margin of safety for a macroeconomic stumble or an unexpected geopolitical escalation.
Opportunities * AI Infrastructure and Energy Beneficiaries: Just as the late-1990s telecom boom relied on physical infrastructure, the current AI revolution requires massive power and cooling solutions. Companies with tangible revenues in grid modernization, data center energy generation, and advanced cooling are uniquely positioned to benefit from both the AI capex boom and the elevated energy pricing environment driven by Middle Eastern tensions. * Pricing Power and Free Cash Flow Quality: In a sticky inflation environment where the 10-year yield remains anchored near 4.56%, capital will increasingly reward companies with high gross margins and low capital intensity. Businesses capable of seamlessly passing through elevated input costs without losing market share will justify their premium multiples through sheer free cash flow generation, separating true quality from speculative growth.
Portfolio Recommendation * Suggested US Growth Stock Exposure: 50-75%: The earnings momentum in AI and tech is undeniably real, mirroring the legitimate technological shifts of past bull markets, which justifies maintaining a heavy growth allocation to capture the ongoing infrastructure supercycle. However, the extreme P/E ratios, the $96 oil shock, and the un-inverting yield curve dictate that we cannot remain fully exposed to the mercy of a potential liquidity or geopolitical shock. A 50-75% allocation allows us to participate in the secular AI boom while preserving enough dry powder to deploy if the geopolitical risk premium forces a broader market correction.
